segments.text: A cost-first view, with revenue as a second branch.
Is that structure MECE, and which branch would you prioritize first, and why?
MECE means mutually exclusive, collectively exhaustive.
Coming back to your structure: what might be missing from your structure?
I'll come back to COGS as a percent of revenue shortly.
Let me make it concrete: of the areas you've named, which one would you check first, and why?
Coming back to what you asked for earlier: COGS is 58% of revenue today, up from 42% two years ago.
With that in hand, what does it tell you, and what would you want to look at
A sixteen-point rise, and a relative increase on top.
Coffee beans were 25% of COGS two years ago.
Taking what you now have on the COGS composition, what do you conclude about what's driving the increase, and what would you check next?
I don't have coffee beans' share of COGS today.
What else would you pull to work out what is driving the COGS increase, and why?
Other input costs — dairy, packaging, and food — are up 37.5% over the past two years. Overhead and rent are 14% of revenue, up slightly from 12%.
With those figures, what do they tell you about where the margin decline is coming from, and how would you test it further?
Menu prices have not changed in two years.
With that pricing information, what does it tell you about the revenue branch, and how does it change where you'd look next?
A volume check.

200 stores today — and it was 200 stores two years ago, so the footprint hasn’t changed. The average transaction is $6.80, up from $6.20 two years ago — about a 10% increase, because customers are buying more items per visit.
With those figures, what do they tell you about how the revenue growth came about, and does that change where you'd focus?
